clean_checkout.why: Plan item 19.1.4 asks for all repository gates from a clean checkout. Every phase to date ran its gates inside a git worktree that already carried .venv directories, __pycache__ and node_modules. Phase 11 exported exactly the tracked plus untracked-non-ignored source set - 1006 files, digest-verified against the worktree, with no .git, no virtualenv, no node_modules and no build output - and ran every gate there from scratch.
clean_checkout.method: git ls-files -z plus git ls-files --others --exclude-standard -z, piped through tar into an empty directory; SHA-256 of all 1006 files compared against the worktree (0 mismatches)

clean_checkout.root_cause: A single cause, not 21 defects. engine/worker/provenance.py:68 engine_identity() uses settings.ENGINE_GIT_SHA, falls back to `git rev-parse HEAD`, and raises ValueError('ENGINE_GIT_SHA or ENGINE_IMAGE_DIGEST is required') when neither is available; engine/worker/tasks.py:1001 converts that into EvaluationFailure('provenance_unavailable'). tools/tests/test_secret_scanning.py:70 separately shells out to `git ls-files '*.example'`.

clean_checkout.verdict: The gates pass from a clean checkout provided the checkout is a git repository or ENGINE_GIT_SHA is supplied. CI's actions/checkout satisfies this, so no CI job is affected today. The runtime DOES declare the requirement - engine/worker_entrypoint.sh:6 calls engine_identity() before starting Celery, and Phase 3's handoff documents the identity sources - so the gap is narrower than it first appeared and lives in the TEST environment: no suite supplies an identity fixture or preflight, and ten phases of green runs all silently depended on being inside a git worktree. Recorded as P11-OWN-02 at medium severity after Codex refuted the broader claim.

SAST.CodeQL: CORRECTED. ci.security.yml IS path-filtered to security/** on both push and pull_request, but it is NOT the repository's only CodeQL workflow: ci.backend-api.yml:36-43, ci.engine.yml:31-37 and ci.frontend.yml:31-38 each run codeql-action/init and codeql-action/analyze on `pull_request: branches: [main]` with no path filter. CodeQL therefore IS a pull-request gate for backend-api/, engine/ and frontend/. Phase 11's original finding to the contrary (P11-OWN-10) was refuted by Codex and is withdrawn in full. ci.security.yml's filter is what its own comment says: that workflow exists only to scan the unmaintained security/ TPRM module.
